description: USA National Phenology Network is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USGS, United States Geological Survey; University of Arizona; USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Phenology is the study of seasonal changes in plants and animals from year to year. This network is a national-scale monitoring and research initiative focused on collecting, organizing, and delivering phenological data and forecasts to support natural resource management and decision-making. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Vector-Borne Disease. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
